correctness.rationale: The indicator covariance identity is exact for independent pollinator failures. Equal row degrees cancel all one-plant terms; equal column degrees force the double root at complete failure. The remaining three finite bipartition cases are checked by complete enumeration with independently computed inclusion-exclusion matrix counts. Quotient-polynomial sets are short and strictly one-signed on the open probability interval. Two connected nine-species webs have equal two-guild degree multisets but variance difference exactly 2q²(1−q)²(1−2q). Complete 32-outcome rational replay verifies the witness moments. The infinite probability interval is treated analytically, not inferred from grid tests.

evidence: Campbell et al. (2012), accepted manuscript of DOI 10.1103/PhysRevE.86.021924, Methods B-C and Results, examine degree-preserving configuration nulls in a dynamic Boolean system; no theorem about the static failure-variance curve is stated.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2018 crossover varies a biological extinction-threshold model and cumulative robustness score, whereas the present crossover varies independent loss probability while preserving the expected instantaneous plant extinction count exactly. The two statements do not imply each other. The 2012 dynamic results, though degree-controlled, do not supply a first finite cardinality for degree-matched static variance reversal.

originality.rationale: Primary papers were examined for whether they already imply the same degree-matched variance crossing and sharp minimum. Their extinction orderings, Boolean dynamics, and integrated knockout-robustness observables differ. Related exact regular incidence-web variance optimization does not cover the irregular matched-degree reversal. Several indexed synonym searches returned no decisive equivalent, though search absence is not proof; alternate network-reliability terminology remains a genuine bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A previously published graph-reliability, random set-coverage, or combinatorial-incidence classification might use different names and imply the finite nine-species threshold. No universal priority proof is claimed.
The ecological model excludes non-independent pollinator extinctions, multispecies feedback and demographic persistence; no empirical transfer is asserted.

value.rationale: The exact first possible total number of species isolates an ecologically meaningful uncertainty-ordering reversal after fully controlling both guilds’ degree distributions and thus all expected plant losses. A factorized crossover at q=1/2 shows how motif-level covariance—not mean susceptibility or degrees—changes the risk ranking when loss intensity varies. The natural coextinction process and fixed-margin comparison motivate this finite cutoff beyond a routine data lookup.
